messages.text: New AI feature: inline suggestions in the editor. The model is tuned; I need copy and behavior that feel right to users. Can we align?
I'd love to. What does the model output today—raw text, or structured (e.g. tone, length)?
Structured. We have intent and snippet. But the placeholder text when it's loading is generic. I want something that doesn't feel robotic.
Loading state matters. Can we show a short, friendly line like 'Thinking…' or 'One moment' instead of 'Generating'? And what happens when it fails?
We retry once, then show an error. Right now the error is technical—'Model timeout.' Users don't care.
They need to know what to do. Something like 'Suggestion didn't load. You can keep typing or try again.' And a soft retry control, not a scary message.
I'll add a 'retry' intent so the UI can show that. What about when the suggestion is borderline—e.g. low confidence? Show it or hide it?
Show it, but visually de-emphasized—maybe lighter text and a small 'Replace' so they know it's optional. Hiding feels like we're deciding for them.
Makes sense. I'll expose a confidence score so you can style it. And I'll tune the prompt so we get fewer low-confidence suggestions over time.
Deal. Send me the copy strings when they're ready; I'll fit them into the design system. This could feel really human.
